We provide services for justice-impacted individuals.

resources.address: 152-18 Union Turnpike, Apt 11o, Flushing, New York 11367
resources.mission: We are a Human Rights organization that serves communities through awareness programs, services, community events education, advocacy, legislation and policy engagement.

resources.name: Bengali Interfaith Youth Empowerment (BIYE)
resources.mission: BIYE empowers Bengali and South Asian youth ages 13-24 through free, trauma-informed programs rooted in mental health, cultural identity, and interfaith dialogue. Guided by the spirit of seva (selfless service), we foster healing, leadership, and community resilience. Our work centers youth voices to build a more compassionate and inclusive future.

resources.name: Divya Jyoti Jagrati Kendra
resources.mission: We help individuals find inner peace and live their fullest selves through Brahm Gyan, the technique for SelfRealization. The journey begins outward and moves inward, passing through the layers of body, breath, mind, wisdom, and bliss to reach the light of the Soul. Wherever you are on this path, we offer the tools and guidance to support your spiritual growth. Weekly spiritual discourses: Sundays, 11am-1pm. Yoga classes: First Saturday of each month.
resources.languages: Hindi, Punjabi, Gujarati, English, Spanish, French

resources.name: Indian Diaspora Council
resources.mission: Indian Diaspora Council is global non-profit organization established September 3, 1997 with the objective to embrace, engage and enhance the shared heritage, aspirations and interests of persons of Indian origin with optimum inclusivity.

resources.name: Maya Smiles Project
resources.mission: The Maya Smiles Project's mission is to help empower all children by providing the basic necessities to attend school.

resources.name: Practical Knowledge, Inc.
resources.mission: Practical Knowledge, Inc. empowers college-bound students from under-resourced communities with the tools, strategies, and confidence to pursue higher education without unnecessary debt. We provide scholarship preparedness workshops, campus-acclimation programming, and other educational resources that equip students to thrive academically and personally. Our mission is to bridge opportunity gaps by delivering practical, actionable knowledge that drives lasting success in education and beyond.
resources.fees: Clients are charged nominal fees to help cover program costs.

resources.name: Queens Centers for Progress
resources.mission: Queens Centers for Progress is dedicated to supporting children and adults with developmental disabilities through person-centered services that nurture independence, strengthen community connections, and enhance quality of life. We also have Workforce Development services for our adult participants.
resources.fees: No, but clients must be pre-approved through DOE or OPWDD in order to receive services.

resources.name: Rabbinical Seminary of America
resources.mission: To educate young people for careers in Jewish Communal Leadership positions. Our alumni graduate with the talents, skills and training to serve the community in every facet of leadership, as teachers, principals, youth workers, chaplains, communal rabbis, and campus college advisors. They currently serve in over 120 communities throughout the USA. We accept young men of the Jewish faith.

resources.name: Samaritan Daytop Village
resources.mission: For 65 years, Samaritan Daytop Village has been improving the quality of life for New Yorkers facing adversity by helping people help themselves. We are nationally recognized for our treatment of substance use disorder as well as for the veteranspecific approach we pioneered. Our continuum of services includes health and mental health care, transitional and supportive housing, educational and vocational assistance, peer-assisted recovery, and specialized programs for adolescents, families, and seniors.
resources.fees: When clients enter treatment, they will meet with a Benefits Specialist who will work with them on payment options. If a client does not have healthcare benefits, the Benefits Specialist will help the client apply for public assistance to cover the cost of treatment. Clients who receive other benefit payments will have their health insurance charged the same rate as clients who receive public assistance.

resources.name: Samaritan Daytop Village
resources.mission: For 65 years, Samaritan Daytop Village has been improving the quality of life for New Yorkers facing adversity by helping people help themselves. We are nationally recognized for our treatment of substance use disorder as well as for the veteran-specific approach we pioneered. Our continuum of services includes health and mental health care, transitional and supportive housing, educational and vocational assistance, peerassisted recovery, and specialized programs for adolescents, families, and seniors. Annually, Samaritan Daytop Village serves over 43,000 people at more than 80 programs throughout New York City, Long Island, and the Hudson Valley. Families who want to enroll their children at The Daytop Preparatory School (DPS) must first schedule an appointment for a clinical assessment with an admissions specialist. DPS Admissions can be contacted at 845.353.2730 for Rockland and 631.351.7112 for Suffolk. All calls are confidential.
resources.fees: School tuition for The Daytop Preparatory School is paid for by the students' home school districts. Most major medical insurance and all Medicaid and managed care plans are accepted for treatment costs.

resources.name: Samaritan Daytop Village
resources.mission: For 65 years, Samaritan Daytop Village has been improving the quality of life for New Yorkers facing adversity by helping people help themselves. We are nationally recognized for our treatment of substance use disorder as well as for the veteran-specific approach we pioneered. Our continuum of services includes health and mental health care, transitional and supportive housing, educational and vocational assistance, peer-assisted recovery, and specialized programs for adolescents, families, and seniors. Annually, Samaritan Daytop Village serves over 43,000 people at more than 80 programs throughout New York City, Long Island, and the Hudson Valley. Healthcare services are integrated into all of our residential treatment and housing programs. To learn more about the primary care services we offer housing clients and the public, visit samaritanvillage.org/get-support/ primary-health-services.
resources.fees: Samaritan Daytop Health accepts most major healthcare insurance as well as Medicare and Medicaid. Regardless of age, you may be eligible for a reduced cost for our healthcare services through Slide Fee Scale.
